what_happened: The job to turn job planning on in athena.toml and record the decision was rejected. The verifier found 6 of 7 criteria met and one unmet: the planning stage's code must stay unchanged, with no file under crates/ differing except the test helper in athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs. One major finding says two other files changed: crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs. The event lists no failed checks. The job went beyond a config change and edited code, probably to make the new setting work or to fix a test.
cause: The scope limit lives only as a prose acceptance criterion that the verifier reads at the end. The producer has no machine-checked list of allowed paths, so it can edit code files while pursuing the outcome, and nothing stops or flags that during the run. Turning planning on likely touched pinned tests or config parsing (run_pin_tests.rs, config.rs) that the config change affected. The job had no rule telling it to stop and report rather than edit. The system therefore finds the overreach only after the work is done.
prevention: When a reading contains a "no files outside X changed" criterion, turn it into an allowed-path list stored with the job. Before the producer hands off, and again before verification, a code check compares the diff's changed files against that list. It fails early with the offending paths, so the producer can revert them or stop and report that the config change needs code changes. This also tells the operator when a config-only goal cannot be reached without code edits.
proposed_request: Turn job planning on in athena.toml and record the decision in the decisions log. Change only athena.toml and the decision record. Do not edit any file under crates/ except the test helper in athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs. If turning planning on makes a test in crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs fail, or needs a change to the config handling in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, do not edit those files. Stop and report which check fails and why, so the code change can be requested as a separate job. Before finishing, list the changed files and confirm that each one is on the allowed list.
